title: Sereja and Algorithm
statementMd:
Sereja loves all sorts of algorithms. He has recently come up with a new algorithm, which receives a string as an input. Let's represent the input string of the algorithm as $*q* = *q*_{1}*q*_{2}... *q*_{*k*}$. The algorithm consists of two steps:

1. Find any continuous subsequence (substring) of three characters of string $*q*$, which doesn't equal to either string "`zyx`", "`xzy`", "`yxz`". If $*q*$ doesn't contain any such subsequence, terminate the algorithm, otherwise go to step 2.
2. Rearrange the letters of the found subsequence randomly and go to step 1.

Sereja thinks that the algorithm works correctly on string $*q*$ if there is a non-zero probability that the algorithm will be terminated. But if the algorithm anyway will work for infinitely long on a string, then we consider the algorithm to work incorrectly on this string.

Sereja wants to test his algorithm. For that, he has string $*s* = *s*_{1}*s*_{2}... *s*_{*n*}$, consisting of $*n*$ characters. The boy conducts a series of $*m*$ tests. As the $*i*$-th test, he sends substring $*s*_{*l*_{*i*}}*s*_{*l*_{*i*} + 1}... *s*_{*r*_{*i*}}$ $(1 ≤ *l*_{*i*} ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ *n*)$ to the algorithm input. Unfortunately, the implementation of his algorithm works too long, so Sereja asked you to help. For each test $(*l*_{*i*}, *r*_{*i*})$ determine if the algorithm works correctly on this test or not.

## Input

The first line contains non-empty string $*s*$, its length ($*n*$) doesn't exceed $10^{5}$. It is guaranteed that string $*s*$ only contains characters: '`x`', '`y`', '`z`'.

The second line contains integer $*m*$ $(1 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{5})$ — the number of tests. Next $*m*$ lines contain the tests. The $*i*$-th line contains a pair of integers $*l*_{*i*}$, $*r*_{*i*}$ $(1 ≤ *l*_{*i*} ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ *n*)$.

## Output

For each test, print "`YES`" (without the quotes) if the algorithm works correctly on the corresponding test and "`NO`" (without the quotes) otherwise.

## Note

In the first example, in test one and two the algorithm will always be terminated in one step. In the fourth test you can get string "`xzyx`" on which the algorithm will terminate. In all other tests the algorithm doesn't work correctly.
statementZhMd:
Sereja 喜欢各种各样的算法。他最近想出了一个新算法，该算法接收一个字符串作为输入。我们将算法的输入字符串表示为 $*q* = *q*_{1}*q*_{2}... *q*_{*k*}$。该算法由以下两个步骤组成：

1. 在字符串 $*q*$ 中找到任意一个长度为 3 的连续子序列（子串），且该子串不等于 "`zyx`"、"`xzy`" 或 "`yxz`"。如果 $*q*$ 不包含这样的子序列，则终止算法；否则进入第 2 步。
2. 随机重排找到的子序列中的字母，然后返回第 1 步。

Sereja 认为，如果算法存在以非零概率终止的可能，那么算法在字符串 $*q*$ 上运行正确。但是，如果算法在某个字符串上无论如何都会无限运行，那么我们认为算法在该字符串上运行不正确。

Sereja 想要测试他的算法。为此，他有一个由 $*n*$ 个字符组成的字符串 $*s* = *s*_{1}*s*_{2}... *s*_{*n*}$。男孩进行了 $*m*$ 次测试。在第 $*i*$ 次测试中，他将子串 $*s*_{*l*_{*i*}}*s*_{*l*_{*i*} + 1}... *s*_{*r*_{*i*}}$ $(1 ≤ *l*_{*i*} ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ *n*)$ 作为算法的输入。不幸的是，他的算法实现运行时间过长，因此 Sereja 请你帮忙。对于每次测试 $( *l*_{*i*}, *r*_{*i*})$，判断算法在这次测试中是否运行正确。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个非空字符串 $*s*$，其长度（$*n*$）不超过 $10^{5}$。保证字符串 $*s*$ 只包含以下字符：'`x`'、'`y`'、'`z`'。

第二行包含一个整数 $*m*$ $(1 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{5})$，表示测试次数。接下来的 $*m*$ 行中，每行包含一次测试。第 $*i*$ 行包含一对整数 $*l*_{*i*}$、$*r*_{*i*}$ $(1 ≤ *l*_{*i*} ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ *n*)$。

## 输出格式

对于每次测试，如果算法在对应测试中运行正确，则输出 "`YES`"（不含引号）；否则输出 "`NO`"（不含引号）。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，第一次和第二次测试中，算法总会在一步内终止。在第四次测试中，可以得到字符串 "`xzyx`"，算法将在该字符串上终止。在其他所有测试中，算法都运行不正确。
